II p105.text: Composition is that Rule or Method in Painting, whereby the several Parts in a Picture are joined together in order to form a Whole. The greatest Subject of Picture is History; the Parts of History are Bodies; the Parts of a Body are the Members; the Parts of the Members are Superficies.

research_update: Selected Italian witness is Alberti’s authorial Italian recension, not Bartoli’s later translation of the Latin. A research reader traced Bartoli’s different Italian translation to 1568 and the du Fresne reprint to 1651, but did not inspect the relevant 1568/1651 pages or establish the full exact transmission chain. In the printed English first occurrence greatest Subject of Picture shifts the Italian grandissima opera del pictore toward a subject of painting; in order to form a Whole is an added rendering. Met attributes the 1726 English translation to Ozell; 1726 and 1755 passages were not compared. The site transcription states one 1755 scan and long-s normalization but does not identify the scan or its own licence. This is research, not formal review.
